title: Understanding PrEP
intro: Before you compare your options, let's start with the basics. Here you'll learn what PrEP is, who it's for, and get an overview of the three ways you can take it.

sections.title: What is PrEP?
sections.content: PrEP stands for Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis. In simple terms, it's medicine you take before being exposed to HIV to prevent getting it. Think of it like a protective shield - when you use PrEP consistently, it blocks HIV from taking hold in your body if you're ever exposed. PrEP is one of the most effective tools we have for HIV prevention, and it has been safely used by millions of people around the world.
keyPoints: PrEP is medicine you take to prevent HIV before you're exposed
It is safe, well-studied, and used by millions of people worldwide
PrEP does not protect against other sexually transmitted infections (STIs) - only HIV
You need a prescription from a healthcare provider to get PrEP
There are now several different ways to take PrEP - you get to choose what works best for you

sections.title: Who Can Benefit from PrEP?
sections.content: PrEP can be a good option for anyone who wants extra protection against HIV. You don't need to be in a specific category or meet a checklist - if preventing HIV matters to you, PrEP may be right for you. Many people from all walks of life use PrEP, including people in relationships where one partner is living with HIV, people who want peace of mind, and people who may not always use condoms.
keyPoints: Anyone who wants to protect themselves from HIV can talk to a provider about PrEP
PrEP is for people who are HIV-negative and want to stay that way
You don't need to explain or justify your reasons for wanting PrEP
PrEP is widely recommended and supported by major health organizations
Your provider can help you decide if PrEP is right for your situation

sections.title: How Does PrEP Protect You?
sections.content: PrEP works by keeping enough HIV-blocking medicine in your body so that if you're ever exposed to the virus, it can't establish an infection. The medicine targets specific steps that HIV needs to copy itself, essentially stopping the virus in its tracks. Different PrEP options use different medications, but they all share the same goal: keeping you HIV-free.
keyPoints: PrEP medicine builds up in the tissues where HIV would enter your body
When enough medicine is present, HIV cannot take hold and multiply
It's important to use PrEP as directed so there's always enough protection in your system
PrEP is not a vaccine - it works as long as you keep taking it

modalityCards.title: Daily Pill
modalityCards.tagline: A pill you take once a day at home

modalityCards.title: On-Demand Pill (2-1-1)
modalityCards.tagline: Pills taken before and after sex, only when you need them

modalityCards.title: Injection Every 2 Months
modalityCards.tagline: A shot at your provider's office every 2 months

modalityCards.title: Injection Every 6 Months
modalityCards.tagline: A shot just twice a year
